title: Modular automorphisms and physical-time KMS conversion

items.title: Spectral analyticity on the modular strip
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator whose spectral projection valued measure $E$ is supported on $(0,\infty)$. For $\xi\in H$, put $\mu_\xi(B)=\langle E(B)\xi,\xi\rangle$. Define
$$D(A^{1/2})=\left\{\xi\in H:\int_{(0,\infty)}\lambda\,d\mu_\xi(\lambda)<\infty\right\}.$$
For $z\in S=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq1\}$ and $\xi\in D(A^{1/2})$, define $A^{-iz/2}\xi$ by the unbounded Borel functional calculus for the function $\lambda\mapsto \exp(-iz\log(\lambda)/2)$. This vector is defined, strongly continuous in $z$ on $S$, and satisfies
$$\|A^{-iz/2}\xi\|^2\leq\|\xi\|^2+\|A^{1/2}\xi\|^2.$$
The map $z\mapsto A^{-iz/2}\xi$ is norm-holomorphic on the open strip $S^\circ$.

references.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras
references.locator: Appendix A, Theorem A.7, printed pp. 146–149

items.title: Strong continuity of positive modular unitary powers
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $A$ be a positive self-adjoint injective operator with spectral projection valued measure $E$ supported on $(0,\infty)$. For $t\in\mathbb R$, the unbounded Borel functional calculus defines $A^{it}$ as a unitary on all of $H$. For every $\xi\in H$, the map $t\mapsto A^{it}\xi$ is norm-continuous.

references.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras

items.title: Upper-strip KMS condition for von Neumann algebras
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M\ne\{0\}$ be a concrete von Neumann algebra on a complex Hilbert space. Use the predual $M_*=Q$ of [[lem-qsmx-von-neumann-predual]]; its elements are the normal linear functionals, and the induced topology $\sigma(M,Q)$ is the ultraweak topology. A **normal state** on $M$ is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:M\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(I)=1$, $\omega(a)\geq0$ for every positive $a\in M$, and
$$\omega\!\left(\sup_i a_i\right)=\sup_i\omega(a_i)$$
for every increasing net $(a_i)$ of positive elements with $0\leq a_i\leq C I$ for a common finite $C$ and supremum taken in $M$.
An automorphism of $M$ is **normal** when it preserves the suprema of all such bounded increasing positive nets.
A **point-ultraweakly continuous one-parameter automorphism group** is a family $(\alpha_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ of bijective unital complex-linear maps $M\to M$ preserving multiplication and adjoints, with $\alpha_0=\operatorname{id}_M$, $\alpha_s\alpha_t=\alpha_{s+t}$, and $t\mapsto\varphi(\alpha_t(x))$ continuous for every $x\in M$ and every normal linear functional $\varphi\in Q$.
For dimensionless $t$ and dimensionless $\beta>0$, the normal state $\omega$ satisfies the **upper-strip $(\alpha,\beta)$ KMS condition** when, for every $A,B\in M$, there is a bounded scalar function $F_{A,B}$ on $S_\beta=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq\beta\}$ that is continuous on $S_\beta$, holomorphic in its interior, and satisfies
$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega(A\alpha_t(B)),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+i\beta)=\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

references.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras
references.locator: §2.2, Definition 2.11, printed pp. 17–18; sign and time reversal stated explicitly here

items.title: Involution and polar identities for the Tomita operator
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in its first argument, let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a concrete von Neumann algebra, and let $\Omega$ be a unit vector that is cyclic and separating for $M$. Define $S_0(x\Omega)=x^*\Omega$ on $M\Omega$ and $F_0(x'\Omega)=x'^*\Omega$ on $M'\Omega$. Let $S=\overline{S_0}$ and $F=S^*$. Then $S$ is a densely defined closed antilinear involution, its polar decomposition is $S=J\Delta^{1/2}$ with $J$ antiunitary and $\Delta$ positive self-adjoint and injective, and
$$J=J^*=J^{-1},\qquad J\Delta J=\Delta^{-1},\qquad J\Delta^{it}J=\Delta^{it}\ (t\in\mathbb R),\qquad F=J\Delta^{-1/2}=\Delta^{1/2}J,\qquad J\Omega=\Omega,\qquad \Delta\Omega=\Omega.$$

references.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras
references.locator: §2.1, Lemma 2.1 and its proof, printed p. 11

references.title: Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory

items.title: Tomita graph and standard modular data
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in its first argument, let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a concrete von Neumann algebra, and let $\Omega$ be a unit vector cyclic and separating for $M$. Define $D(S_0)=M\Omega$ and $S_0(x\Omega)=x^*\Omega$ for $x\in M$. Let $S=\overline{S_0}$ and write its polar decomposition as $S=J\Delta^{1/2}$. The preceding Tomita-operator lemma ensures this closure and polar data are well defined, with $\Delta$ positive self-adjoint and injective. For $x\in\mathcal B(H)$ and dimensionless $t\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\sigma_t(x):=\Delta^{it}x\Delta^{-it}.$$
Set $\omega(x)=\langle x\Omega,\Omega\rangle$. The powers $\Delta^{it}$ are the bounded unitary imaginary powers from the unbounded Borel functional calculus. At this definition stage $\sigma_t$ is defined on $\mathcal B(H)$; preservation of $M$ is established by a separate theorem.

references.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras
Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory

items.title: Faithful matrix modular flow and Gibbs time
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\geq1$, let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^n$, and let $\rho$ be a positive-definite Hermitian matrix, meaning $\langle\rho v,v\rangle>0$ for each nonzero $v\in\mathcal H$, with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Write $\mathcal H_{\rm HS}=M_n(\mathbb C)$ with inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle_{\rm HS}=\operatorname{Tr}(Y^*X)$, linear in the first argument, and let $M_n(\mathbb C)$ act on $\mathcal H_{\rm HS}$ by left multiplication. For $\Omega=\rho^{1/2}$, the standard modular data are
$$JX=X^*,\qquad \Delta X=\rho X\rho^{-1},\qquad \sigma_t(A)=\rho^{it}A\rho^{-it}\quad(A\in M_n(\mathbb C),\ t\in\mathbb R).$$
The vector state of $\Omega$ is $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$. If $H=H^*$ has energy unit joules, $\beta>0$ has unit joules$^{-1}$, $\hbar>0$ has unit joule-seconds, and $\rho=e^{-\beta H}/Z$ with $Z=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})$, then the physical-time dynamics
$$\alpha_s(A)=e^{isH/\hbar}Ae^{-isH/\hbar}\quad(s\text{ in seconds})$$
satisfies
$$\alpha_s=\sigma_{-s/(\beta\hbar)}.$$
On the finite-dimensional C$^*$-algebra $M_n(\mathbb C)$, $\omega$ is a $\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in the physical-time convention of the stated KMS definition, with strip width $\beta\hbar$ seconds. If $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, then $k_B$ has units joules per kelvin and $T$ has units kelvins.

references.title: Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory
F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras
references.locator: §2.1, Example 2.4 and §2.2, Theorem 2.14, printed pp. 11 and 18

items.title: Modular resolvent invariance and commutant equality
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the standard modular data of a concrete von Neumann algebra $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ with unit cyclic-separating vector $\Omega$. Let $F=S^*$, where $S$ is the closure of $S_0(x\Omega)=x^*\Omega$, and let $F_0(x'\Omega)=x'^*\Omega$ on $M'\Omega$. For every $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ with $|\lambda|=1$ and $\lambda\ne-1$,
$$(\Delta+\lambda)^{-1}M'\Omega\subseteq M\Omega.$$
The modular conjugation and operator satisfy
$$JMJ=M',\qquad \Delta^{it}M\Delta^{-it}=M\quad(t\in\mathbb R),\qquad \overline{F_0}=F=S^*.$$

references.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras
references.locator: §2.1, Lemmas 2.5–2.8, Theorem 2.2 and Remark 2.9, printed pp. 12–16

items.title: Tomita modular automorphisms and the upper-strip KMS condition
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a concrete von Neumann algebra and $\Omega$ a unit cyclic-separating vector with standard modular data $(J,\Delta,\sigma_t)$ and vector state $\omega(x)=\langle x\Omega,\Omega\rangle$. Then $\sigma_t(x)=\Delta^{it}x\Delta^{-it}$ restricts to a one-parameter group of normal $*$-automorphisms of $M$ that is point-ultraweakly continuous, and $JMJ=M'$. The vector state $\omega$ is faithful and normal and is an upper-strip $(\alpha,1)$ KMS state, in the definition of the preceding item, for $\alpha_t=\sigma_{-t}$. This is a dimensionless W*-algebra KMS assertion; it does not assert norm continuity of $\sigma_t$ on all of $M$.

references.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras
references.locator: §2.1, Theorem 2.2, printed pp. 11 and 15–16; §2.2, Theorem 2.14, printed pp. 18–19

items.title: Modular frequency requires a physical time identification
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $0<p<1$ and $\rho=\operatorname{diag}(p,1-p)$ on $\mathbb C^2$. Its modular automorphism group acts on the off-diagonal matrix unit by
$$\sigma_t(E_{12})=e^{it\log(p/(1-p))}E_{12}.$$
The modular frequency $\log(p/(1-p))$ is dimensionless and does not specify a physical energy or clock. If one separately supplies a Hamiltonian $H=\operatorname{diag}(E_1,E_2)$ with energies in joules, inverse energy $\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, and action $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds with $\rho=e^{-\beta H}/Z$, then $p/(1-p)=e^{-\beta(E_1-E_2)}$ and the physical angular frequency $(E_1-E_2)/\hbar$ has units seconds$^{-1}$. For $p=\tfrac12$ the modular frequency is zero; for $p\ne\tfrac12$ it is nonzero but still has no physical time unit before this identification.

references.title: Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory
F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras
